title: Gaussian Integral
subtitle: Analysis · Probability
summary: The integral of e^(−x²) over all reals equals √π.
detail:
\[ \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-x^2}\,dx = \sqrt{\pi} \]

Proved by squaring and converting to polar coordinates: \(\left(\int e^{-x^2}dx\right)^2=\iint e^{-(x^2+y^2)}dA=\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^\infty e^{-r^2}r\,dr\,d\theta=\pi\). The normal distribution PDF integrates to 1 via the generalisation \(\int e^{-x^2/(2\sigma^2)}dx=\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}\).
